title: Guide: 3-colourable graphs, blocking
description: Graphs on n nodes that can be 3-coloured; the check looks for a colouring (a witness), and a graph without one is blocked on its own. See the guide page "Checks that look for a witness, and cores".

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.text:
% A candidate: any graph.
{ edge(X,Y) : node(X), node(Y), X < Y }.
#show edge/2.

fragments.name: check
fragments.text:
% A witness, not a counterexample: a proper 3-colouring of the candidate.
% If there is none, the candidate is wrong, and the unsat core says which
% edges are to blame.
1 { col(N,1..3) } 1 :- node(N).
:- edge(X,Y), col(X,C), col(Y,C).
fragments.description: Looks for a proper 3-colouring of the candidate, a witness (solver C).

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# The check looks for a witness: a candidate without one is wrong.
search A:
    on candidate M:
        if not C.solve(assume G(M)):
            reject M with G.block(M)
